beats.say: A fake sign-in window often starts with an email: a document was shared with you, sign in to view it.
The button offers sign-in with a familiar account. The window that opens is drawn inside the site.

subject.text: Kamran Aliyev shared a document with you

beats.say: An email threatening to shut down your office's social media page is the same trap.
The rule: do not sign in through the button in the email. Open the site yourself.

question.prompt: You got this email. What do you do?

options.label: I press the button and sign in with my IshPocht account
options.feedback: The button takes you to a site you do not know. The sign-in window there may be fake.

options.label: I call Kamran on the number I know and ask
options.feedback: Right. If the document is real, Kamran will share it again in your office's own system.

options.label: I forward it to colleagues so they can look too
options.feedback: Then the trap reaches others as well. Send a suspicious email only to technical support.

subject.text: Kamran Aliyev shared a document with you

body.text: The link is valid for 24 hours.

scenes.explain: If the document is real, you will see it when you open the site yourself. You never need the sign-in button in the email.

scenes.title: Your work mail
scenes.intro: Four emails are waiting in your morning mail. Open each one and pick the right action.

subject.text: Narmin Hasanova shared a file with you

body.text: Note: the budget table we discussed this morning.

actions.label: Open file
actions.feedback: You expected this file, and the link goes to the service's own address. It is fine to open.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. A known colleague, an expected file and the service's own address.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Caution is good, but there are no warning signs here. Narmin told you about this file this morning.

subject.text: Kamran Aliyev shared a document with you

body.text: The link is valid for 24 hours.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. A different domain and a sign-in button that led to a fake window.

actions.label: Sign in with IshPocht
actions.feedback: The page would have drawn an IshPocht window and asked for your password. Do not touch buttons like this.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Deleting works too. If you report it, technical support can warn your colleagues.

subject.text: Your page will be removed within 24 hours

body.text: A copyright violation was found on your office's official page.
To appeal, sign in as the page administrator:
Without a reply, the page will be closed for good.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. A real warning would also appear inside the social network's own app.

actions.label: Appeal
actions.feedback: The appeal page drew a Kontakto window and collected the password and the code. Your office's page would go to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply: this is a mistake
actions.feedback: The scammer reads the reply and sends a new link. Report the email instead.

body.text: Today between 19:00 and 20:00, work mail may be unavailable for a few minutes.
No action is needed from you.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. It comes from an internal address, with no link and no request for a password.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: This email has no link and asks for nothing. Notices like this are normal work.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: That is fine, the email only informs you. There is no danger.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs that this sign-in window is fake.

body.text: Also enter the code you got by SMS
The window does not move past the edge of the page

spots.label: Real address
spots.explain: The browser's own address bar shows a different site. Look at that, not at the text inside the window.

spots.label: Painted address
spots.explain: This address bar is part of the window's picture. The scammer can write anything there.

spots.label: Verification code
spots.explain: They want the code to get past two-step verification. Never type a code into a window like this.

spots.label: Window stuck
spots.explain: A real window can be dragged outside the browser. This one stays stuck inside the page.

spots.label: Pressure
spots.explain: The countdown is there to make you sign in without checking.

points: Find a shared document by opening the site yourself
An email threatening to close your page is a trap
If you typed your password, change it now and tell technical support
